chapter: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
title: Lu's record labels and Sammy Price's blues sessions
summary: Lu lists her labels, Vocalion, Decca, Apollo and Capitol, and Milt recalls Sammy Price recording blues singers for $30.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: When I worked at Apollo, you know, after Decca... You know, I made that Vocalion record, then I worked for Decca, then I worked for Apollo, and then I worked for Capitol. Then I made records for the States(?), and other records around here.
Mel Williams was at Decca, wasn't he.

Sammy Price used to work for those people. Because see, that was my introduction to the record industry. Sammy Price took me... I made a lot of those records with Georgia White, a Blues singer... Remember Georgia White, the Blues singer from the South?
Johnny Temple... I made quite a few of those things with Sam Price...
He'd bring them in, yeah. That was Mel Williams' right-hand man.

Yeah, he used to go down South and get them and bring them in, and get a bunch of sandwiches and a case of beer and whiskey, and we'd lock up in there all day -- and he would bring them in. He'd bring in... We'd do some Blues with a singer...
Yeah, or male singers. Same Blues... We did ...(?)....(?)... And we'd just there and got $30 and went on home very happy.
